newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Avia Presto will not introduce new fee at Rotterdam.
newsitem.headline: Avia Presto will not introduce new fee at Rotterdam.

text.p: Dutch handling company Avia Presto is not introducing a new controversial handling fee at Rotterdam airport, where it is the main ground handler, Avia Presto spokesman, Paul Maarsman said.
Dutch handling companies have been testing market reaction to a new 35 guilder fee which is due to be introduced on July 1.
However it will be applying the new fee -- which has been widely condemned by airlines and shippers -- at Amsterdam's Schiphol airport.
Handlers claim that they are having to do more administration work as a significant amount of cargo is heavier when it arrives at the handling company than the booked weight on the airwaybill.
If a consignment is between three to six percent heavier, the 35 guilder fee is then charged directly to the forwarding agents.
In the future, the fee may be charged directly to the airlines, he said and this possibility is still consideration.
Maarsman said he is not expecting cargo to be re-routed via Rotterdam in a bid to avoid the charge.
He added that the fee is not as necessary at Rotterdam because most of the cargo is perishable traffic and simpler to handle.
The Schiphol airfreight community is in the main, ridding itself of a separate 15 guilder acceptance fee which is a flat fee charged to forwarders by the handlers for accepting cargo.
This is now expected to be abandoned on July 1 after several years of wrangling over the charge, industry sources said.
Avia Presto will retain this 15 guilder charge at Rotterdam, although it may be in a different form, said Maarsman. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com"
